question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error.

Several days later, / he received a written / comeunication from the magistrate / that the case has been dropped.
option_4: that the case has been dropped
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. comeunication from the magistrate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The third segment contains the misspelt word "comeunication". The correct spelling is "communication" — COM + MU + NI + CA + TION, with a double "m" and the vowel "u" (not "e") in the second syllable.

◦ Correct: Several days later, he received a written communication from the magistrate that the case has been dropped.

• "Communication" means the act of conveying or exchanging information, news or ideas. (संचार / सूचना का आदान-प्रदान)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 "Several days later," is correctly spelt ("several", "later").

• Segment 2 "he received a written" is correct — note the "ei" after c rule in "received".

• Segment 4 "that the case has been dropped" is correct — "dropped" doubles the final "p" before "-ed" (CVC rule).

NOTE

• Words from the same family: communicate, communicative, communicable, communiqué, community. All keep the double "m".

• Commonly misspelt SSC words of this pattern: accommodation, recommend, occassion (wrong) → occasion, embarrassment, millennium.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A man whose wife is dead
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Widower.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Widower" is the exact one-word substitute for a man whose wife is dead (and who has not remarried). (विधुर)

◦ Example: After his wife's death he lived as a widower for twenty years.

• The -er ending marks the masculine form; the feminine counterpart is "widow".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Ascetic" — a person who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from worldly pleasures. (तपस्वी)

• Option 3 "Widow" — a woman whose husband is dead. (विधवा) — the gender is reversed here.

• Option 4 "Bachelor" — an unmarried man; he has never married, so his case is not that of a dead wife. (कुँवारा)

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes frequently asked in SSC:

◦ Spinster — an unmarried woman past the usual age for marriage.

◦ Orphan — a child whose parents are dead.

◦ Celibate — one who abstains from marriage/sexual relations.

◦ Misogamist — one who hates marriage; Misogynist — one who hates women.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

No sooner did he finished his examination than he left for his cricket training centre.
option_3: no sooner than he did finished
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. no sooner did he finish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "No sooner" is a negative adverbial placed at the beginning of a sentence, so it compels inversion — the auxiliary comes before the subject: "No sooner did he ...".

• After the do-support auxiliary "did", the verb must be in the bare infinitive (V1) — "finish", never "finished".

◦ Correct: No sooner did he finish his examination than he left for his cricket training centre.

• "No sooner" is always correlated with "than" (never with "when" or "then").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "no sooner than he finished" and Option 3 "no sooner than he did finished" wrongly place "than" immediately after "no sooner" and drop the inversion.

• Option 4 "no sooner had he finish" is wrong because after "had" the past participle (V3) is required — "had finished", not "had finish".

NOTE

• Both these forms are acceptable in English: "No sooner did he finish ... than ..." and "No sooner had he finished ... than ...". The examination tests whether the auxiliary and the verb form agree.

• Other negative openers that force inversion: Hardly / Scarcely ... when, Seldom, Never, Rarely, Not only ... but also, Little did I know.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

They will start their journey after the breakfast.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. after the breakfast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Names of meals — breakfast, lunch, dinner, supper, tea — are used without any article when they refer to the meal in general.

◦ Correct: They will start their journey after breakfast.

• Hence "after the breakfast" is wrong; the definite article "the" must be dropped.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "They" is a correct plural subject; Option 1 "will start" is the correct simple future form; Option 2 "their journey" correctly uses the possessive adjective "their" agreeing with "They".

NOTE

• The article is used with meals when the meal is particularised or described by an adjective:

◦ "The breakfast we had at the hotel was excellent." (particular meal)

◦ "We had a heavy breakfast." (qualified by an adjective)

• Similar zero-article categories: languages (He speaks English), games (They play cricket), and diseases in general (He suffers from fever).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Legandry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Legandry" is incorrectly spelt. The correct spelling is "legendary" — LE + GEN + DA + RY, formed from the noun "legend" + "-ary".

• "Legendary" means remarkably famous; described in legends. (पौराणिक / अत्यंत प्रसिद्ध)

◦ Example: Sachin Tendulkar is a legendary cricketer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Wholeness" (the state of being whole/complete) is correctly spelt — whole + ness, the "w" is silent.

• Option 2 "Overwhelming" (very great in amount; overpowering) is correctly spelt — over + whelm + ing.

• Option 4 "Inclusive" (containing everything; not excluding any group) is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Remember the base word to fix the spelling: legend → legendary. The vowel is "e", not "a", and the ending is "-ary", not "-ry".

• Other "-ary" words often misspelt: necessary, secretary, dictionary, complimentary, voluntary, imaginary.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Humane
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cruel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Humane" (adjective) means showing compassion, kindness and mercy, especially towards people and animals in distress. (दयालु / मानवीय)

◦ Example: The rescue team gave the injured animals humane treatment.

• Its exact opposite is "Cruel" — wilfully causing pain or suffering; merciless. (क्रूर / निर्दयी)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Kind" is a synonym of humane, not an antonym — a classic trap option.

• Option 1 "Proud" (feeling deep satisfaction or arrogance) and Option 4 "Imperfect" (having faults) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of humane: compassionate, merciful, benevolent, sympathetic, benign, kind-hearted.

• Antonyms of humane: cruel, brutal, barbarous, inhumane, merciless, ruthless, savage.

• Do not confuse humane (compassionate) with human (relating to mankind) and humanistic (concerned with human welfare/values).

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Prevention.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Prevention" — PRE + VEN + TION. It is the noun formed from the verb "prevent" by adding the suffix "-ion" (prevent → prevent + ion → prevention).

• "Prevention" means the act of stopping something from happening. (रोकथाम / निवारण)

◦ Example: Prevention is better than cure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Prevenseon", 3 "Previnsion" and 4 "Prevension" are all misspellings — they wrongly use "-seon", "-sion" or the vowel "i" in place of "e".

NOTE

• Verbs ending in "-vent", "-tent", "-cent" form nouns in "-tion": prevent → prevention, invent → invention, intent → intention, retent → retention.

• Useful static reference: the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) and the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 all use this spelling.

question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

He is good at playing the guitar than his brother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is better.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contains the word "than", which is the signal of the comparative degree. A positive-degree adjective such as "good" cannot be used with "than".

• The comparative form of "good" is irregular: good → better → best. Hence "is good ... than" must become "is better ... than".

◦ Correct: He is better at playing the guitar than his brother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "in playing" is wrong — the fixed collocation is "good/better AT (doing) something", never "in playing".

• Option 3 "guitar" is wrong — names of musical instruments take the definite article: play the guitar, play the piano, play the flute.

• Option 4 "to" is wrong — "better" is followed by "than"; only Latin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior, preferable) take "to".

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison of irregular adjectives: good/well – better – best; bad/ill – worse – worst; little – less – least; much/many – more – most; far – farther/further – farthest/furthest.

• Note the contrast: "He is good at cricket." (no comparison) vs "He is better at cricket than I am." (comparison).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

The company is looking for some ______________(idle) workers who can join the organisation immediately.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. diligent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Idle" means lazy; not working; avoiding work. (आलसी / निष्क्रिय)

• Its antonym is "diligent" — hard-working, showing careful and persistent effort. (परिश्रमी / मेहनती)

◦ Correct: The company is looking for some diligent workers who can join the organisation immediately.

• The context also demands a positive quality: a company would obviously want hard-working employees.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "coy" — shy or pretending to be shy/modest. (शर्मीला)

• Option 3 "callous" — emotionally hard, showing no sympathy for others. (निष्ठुर)

• Option 4 "sober" — serious, sensible, not drunk. (संयत / शांत)

None of these is the opposite of "idle".

NOTE

• Synonyms of idle: lazy, indolent, slothful, inactive, unoccupied, lethargic.

• Antonyms of idle: diligent, industrious, hard-working, assiduous, sedulous, busy.

• Do not confuse idle (lazy) with idol (an image/object of worship) — a very common SSC homophone pair.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

He simply continued to say something in order to convey information in a calm voice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. speak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Speak" means to say something in order to convey information, an opinion or a feeling — this is the standard dictionary definition, which matches the underlined group of words exactly.

◦ Correct: He simply continued to speak in a calm voice. (बोलना)

• The phrase "in a calm voice" further confirms simple speaking, not any specialised act.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dictate" — to say words aloud so that another person may write them down, or to give orders authoritatively. (श्रुतलेख देना / हुक्म चलाना) It adds a meaning not present in the given phrase.

• Option 2 "teach" — to impart knowledge or skill to a learner. (पढ़ाना)

• Option 4 "spell" — to name or write the letters of a word in order. (वर्तनी बताना)

NOTE

• Compare the shades of meaning: speak (to utter words), talk (to converse), say (to state, needs an object), tell (to inform someone, needs an indirect object), narrate (to relate a story), address (to speak formally to an audience).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

After years of rivalry, the two families decided to bury the hatchet.
option_2: To end a quarrel by never talking to each other
option_3: To end a quarrel and become friendly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To end a quarrel and become friendly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bury the hatchet" means to make peace; to end a quarrel or conflict and become friends again. (पुरानी दुश्मनी भुलाकर मेल कर लेना)

◦ Example: After years of rivalry, the two families decided to bury the hatchet and attend the wedding together.

• The context — "After years of rivalry ... decided to" — clearly signals reconciliation, so Option 3 is the only fit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To continue an old quarrel" and Option 4 "To start a new quarrel" are the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2 "To end a quarrel by never talking to each other" is a distractor — burying the hatchet implies friendly relations resume, not silence.

NOTE

• Origin: the phrase comes from a Native American custom of literally burying weapons (hatchets/tomahawks) in the ground when tribes agreed to peace.

• Similar idioms of reconciliation: "make up", "hold out an olive branch", "mend fences", "let bygones be bygones", "patch up".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Did / her friend / went to / school yesterday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. went to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In an interrogative sentence formed with the auxiliary "did", the main verb must be in its bare infinitive (V1) form. The tense is already carried by "did", so the main verb is never put in the past form.

◦ Correct: Did her friend go to school yesterday?

• "went" is the past tense (V2) of "go" and cannot follow "did".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment 4 "Did" is the correct auxiliary for a past-tense question.

• Segment 2 "her friend" is a correct singular subject; Segment 3 (option 2) "school yesterday" correctly omits the article — "go to school" is a fixed phrase used without "the" when it refers to attending school.

NOTE

• Rule: Do / Does / Did / Modal + V1. Examples: Did he come? / Does she play? / He did not eat. / She can sing.

• Zero-article institutional phrases: go to school / college / church / bed / hospital / prison — the article appears only when the building itself is meant ("I went to the school to meet the principal").

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The Delhi administration is seriously worried about the warning to civic health posed by the polluted waters of Yamuna.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the threat to civic health.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "posed" collocates naturally with "threat" — the standard English collocation is "pose a threat to", meaning to be a source of danger to. (खतरा उत्पन्न करना)

◦ Correct: The Delhi administration is seriously worried about the threat to civic health posed by the polluted waters of Yamuna.

• "warning" is wrong because a warning is a caution given by someone, whereas polluted water creates a danger, not a caution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a peril" carries the right sense (grave danger) but the indefinite article "a" is wrong here — the sentence points to a specific, known danger, and "posed by the polluted waters of Yamuna" makes it definite.

• Option 2 "the notice" (a formal announcement) does not collocate with "posed".

• Option 3 "the plague" refers to a specific epidemic disease and is far too narrow for "civic health".

NOTE

• Useful collocations with "pose": pose a threat, pose a risk, pose a danger, pose a challenge, pose a problem, pose a question.

• The Yamuna is the largest tributary of the Ganga, rising from the Yamunotri glacier in Uttarakhand — a frequent static-GK link in comprehension passages.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Mohan is respected / by everyone / because he works / hardly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. hardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hardly" is not the adverb form of "hard". It is a negative adverb meaning "scarcely / almost not". Using it here reverses the intended sense — "he works hardly" would mean "he almost does not work", which contradicts "Mohan is respected".

• The correct adverb is "hard", which has the same form as the adjective and means "with great effort".

◦ Correct: Mohan is respected by everyone because he works hard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 (option 4) "Mohan is respected" is a correct present-simple passive.

• Segment 2 (option 1) "by everyone" correctly introduces the agent in the passive voice.

• Segment 3 (option 2) "because he works" is a correct subordinate clause of reason.

NOTE

• Pairs where the "-ly" form changes the meaning completely:

◦ hard (with effort) / hardly (scarcely)

◦ late (not early) / lately (recently)

◦ near (close) / nearly (almost)

◦ short (briefly) / shortly (soon)

◦ high (at a great height) / highly (very much)

• "Hardly", "scarcely" and "barely" are already negative — never use another negative with them ("I cannot hardly see" is wrong).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Day and night
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Continuously.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "day and night" means all the time; continuously; without stopping. (लगातार / दिन-रात)

◦ Example: The engineers worked day and night to repair the bridge before the monsoon.

• The literal joining of "day" + "night" covers the whole 24 hours, hence the sense of uninterrupted continuity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Clumsily" — in an awkward, ungainly manner. (भद्दे ढंग से)

• Option 3 "Adversely" — in a harmful or unfavourable way. (प्रतिकूल रूप से)

• Option 4 "Diligently" — with careful, persistent effort. This is a close trap, but it describes the manner/quality of work, not its non-stop duration, which is what "day and night" expresses.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of continuity: "round the clock", "around the clock", "24/7", "non-stop", "at a stretch", "on and on".

• Other "day"-idioms for SSC: "call it a day" (to stop work), "day in, day out" (every day without change), "have a field day" (to enjoy oneself greatly), "save for a rainy day" (to save for hard times).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Humility
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Arrogance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Humility" (noun) means modesty; a modest view of one's own importance; the absence of pride. (विनम्रता / नम्रता)

• Its direct opposite is "Arrogance" — an offensive display of superiority; excessive pride and self-importance. (अहंकार / घमंड)

◦ Example: Despite his success he showed great humility, never a trace of arrogance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Shyness" — nervousness in the company of others; it is a form of social discomfort, not the opposite of modesty.

• Option 2 "Timidity" — lack of courage or confidence. (कायरता / डरपोकपन)

• Option 4 "Obedience" — compliance with orders; this is closer to a synonym-like quality of humility, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of humility: modesty, meekness, humbleness, unpretentiousness, diffidence.

• Antonyms of humility: arrogance, pride, conceit, haughtiness, vanity, insolence, hubris.

• Adjective forms: humble ↔ arrogant / haughty / conceited / supercilious.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

They had been dancing / for an hour / when our dance teacher / had arrived.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. had arrived.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a past perfect continuous action ("had been dancing") is interrupted by another action, that interrupting action is expressed in the simple past, not in the past perfect.

◦ Correct: They had been dancing for an hour when our dance teacher arrived.

• Using "had arrived" wrongly puts both actions in the perfect tense, destroying the time relationship between them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 (option 2) "They had been dancing" is a correct past perfect continuous.

• Segment 2 (option 3) "for an hour" correctly uses "for" with a period of time and the article "an" before the silent-"h" word "hour".

• Segment 3 (option 1) "when our dance teacher" correctly introduces the time clause.

NOTE

• Structure: had been + V-ing + for/since + time ... when + simple past.

◦ She had been waiting since 5 o'clock when the bus finally came.

• Use "for" with a duration (for two hours, for six years) and "since" with a point of time (since Monday, since 2015).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Jane, please don’t tell me fairy tales; I just want to know the real matter ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. in a nutshell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in a nutshell" means in a few words; briefly; concisely. (संक्षेप में)

◦ Correct: Jane, please don't tell me fairy tales; I just want to know the real matter in a nutshell.

• The speaker rejects long, embellished stories ("fairy tales") and asks for the plain, brief truth — exactly the sense of "in a nutshell".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "out in the cold" means ignored or excluded from a group. (उपेक्षित)

• Option 2 "in a fortnight" simply means within two weeks — a time expression, not a fit here.

• Option 3 "in the long run" means eventually; over a long period of time. (अंततः)

NOTE

• Origin: the expression alludes to something small enough to be written on a surface as tiny as a nutshell.

• Synonymous expressions: "in short", "in brief", "to sum up", "to cut a long story short", "in a word".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The shopkeeper was sly as a fox and tried to sell off the old stock.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. smart and clever.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The simile "(as) sly as a fox" describes a person who is very cunning, crafty and clever, especially in a deceitful way. (लोमड़ी जैसा चालाक)

◦ Example: The shopkeeper was sly as a fox and tried to sell off the old stock to unsuspecting customers.

• The fox is the traditional symbol of cunning in English idiom and fable, which is why the comparison carries the sense of shrewd cleverness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "slow", Option 3 "suspicious" and Option 4 "in confusion or disagreement" have no connection with slyness.

• "Sly" itself means cunning, secretive, deceitful; synonyms are crafty, wily, artful, shrewd, foxy.

NOTE

• Other animal similes commonly tested in SSC:

◦ as blind as a bat, as busy as a bee, as stubborn as a mule, as proud as a peacock

◦ as strong as an ox, as quiet as a mouse, as brave as a lion, as wise as an owl

◦ as slippery as an eel, as gentle as a lamb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Bhanu, the security guard, asks everyone entering my building to show their ________ card.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. identity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Identity card" (commonly shortened to ID card) is the fixed compound expression for a card that shows who a person is. (पहचान पत्र)

◦ Correct: Bhanu, the security guard, asks everyone entering my building to show their identity card.

• A security guard's duty is to verify who a visitor is, so only "identity" fits the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "place card" is a small card marking a person's seat at a dinner table — irrelevant here.

• Option 3 "self card" is not an English expression at all.

• Option 4 "name card" (a visiting/business card) merely gives a name and contact details; it is not proof of identity and is not what a guard would demand.

NOTE

• Note the word class: "identity" is the noun used attributively (identity card, identity proof, identity theft), while "identify" is the verb and "identical" the adjective.

• Common Indian identity documents for general awareness: Aadhaar card (UIDAI), PAN card (Income Tax Department), Voter ID / EPIC (Election Commission of India), Passport (MEA), Driving Licence.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Effective communication is about more than just exchanging information. It's about understanding the emotion and intentions (1)_____ the information. As well as being able to clearly convey a message, you need to also (2)____ in a way that gains the full meaning of what's being said and makes the other person feel heard and understood. For many of us, communicating more clearly and effectively requires learning some (3)_____ skills. Whether you’re trying to improve communication with your spouse, kids, boss, or coworkers, learning these skills can (4)______ your connections to others, build greater trust and respect, and (5)______ teamwork, problem solving, and your overall social and emotional health.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. behind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a preposition meaning "underlying / lying at the back of". The idiomatic expression is "the emotion and intentions behind the information", i.e. the motive that lies behind what is said.

◦ Correct: It's about understanding the emotion and intentions behind the information.

• "Behind" is regularly used in the figurative sense of "responsible for / at the root of": the reason behind the decision, the people behind the plan, the idea behind the scheme.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "in front of" and Options 3 "above" / 4 "below" are purely physical/spatial prepositions and cannot express the abstract idea of an underlying motive.

• The passage contrasts "just exchanging information" with understanding the feelings that motivate it — a clear signal for "behind".

NOTE

• Figurative uses of prepositions worth remembering: the story behind the news, beyond doubt, under pressure, on purpose, in favour of, at stake.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Effective communication is about more than just exchanging information. It's about understanding the emotion and intentions (1)_____ the information. As well as being able to clearly convey a message, you need to also (2)____ in a way that gains the full meaning of what's being said and makes the other person feel heard and understood. For many of us, communicating more clearly and effectively requires learning some (3)_____ skills. Whether you’re trying to improve communication with your spouse, kids, boss, or coworkers, learning these skills can (4)______ your connections to others, build greater trust and respect, and (5)______ teamwork, problem solving, and your overall social and emotional health.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. listen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is built on a contrast: "As well as being able to clearly convey a message, you need to also ______". Conveying a message is the speaking side of communication; the complementary skill is therefore "listen".

◦ Correct: As well as being able to clearly convey a message, you need to also listen in a way that gains the full meaning of what's being said and makes the other person feel heard and understood.

• The phrase "makes the other person feel heard" is the decisive clue — only listening can make somebody feel heard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "talk" and 4 "speak" merely repeat the idea of conveying a message already stated before "as well as", so they add nothing and break the contrast.

• Option 1 "think" does not fit "in a way that gains the full meaning of what's being said", which requires reception of speech.

NOTE

• The passage describes "active listening" — hearing with full attention, understanding the speaker's feelings, and responding so the speaker feels understood.

• Note the difference: hear = to perceive sound (involuntary); listen = to pay attention to sound (deliberate).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Effective communication is about more than just exchanging information. It's about understanding the emotion and intentions (1)_____ the information. As well as being able to clearly convey a message, you need to also (2)____ in a way that gains the full meaning of what's being said and makes the other person feel heard and understood. For many of us, communicating more clearly and effectively requires learning some (3)_____ skills. Whether you’re trying to improve communication with your spouse, kids, boss, or coworkers, learning these skills can (4)______ your connections to others, build greater trust and respect, and (5)______ teamwork, problem solving, and your overall social and emotional health.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. important.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence says that communicating more clearly and effectively "requires learning some ______ skills". Since the whole passage praises these skills — they "build greater trust and respect" and improve "your overall social and emotional health" — the adjective must be positive: "important".

◦ Correct: For many of us, communicating more clearly and effectively requires learning some important skills.

• "Important" means of great significance or value. (महत्वपूर्ण)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "boring" (dull, uninteresting) contradicts the encouraging tone of the passage.

• Option 2 "trivial" means of very little value or importance — the exact opposite of what is required. (तुच्छ)

• Option 3 "wasteful" means using resources carelessly, which makes no sense with "skills". (अपव्ययी)

NOTE

• In cloze tests, always check the tone (positive/negative) of the surrounding sentences before choosing an adjective; here every neighbouring clause is complimentary.

• Synonyms of important: vital, crucial, significant, essential, key, pivotal, indispensable.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Effective communication is about more than just exchanging information. It's about understanding the emotion and intentions (1)_____ the information. As well as being able to clearly convey a message, you need to also (2)____ in a way that gains the full meaning of what's being said and makes the other person feel heard and understood. For many of us, communicating more clearly and effectively requires learning some (3)_____ skills. Whether you’re trying to improve communication with your spouse, kids, boss, or coworkers, learning these skills can (4)______ your connections to others, build greater trust and respect, and (5)______ teamwork, problem solving, and your overall social and emotional health.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. deepen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank governs the object "your connections to others" and is joined by "and" to the positive results "build greater trust and respect". Parallel positive meaning is therefore required, and "deepen" (to make stronger, more intense or more profound) is the exact collocation.

◦ Correct: ... learning these skills can deepen your connections to others, build greater trust and respect ...

• Collocation: deepen a relationship / a bond / a friendship / an understanding. (गहरा करना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hamper" — to hinder or obstruct. (बाधा डालना) Negative, so it contradicts "build greater trust and respect".

• Option 2 "trivialise" — to make something seem less important than it is. (महत्वहीन बनाना)

• Option 3 "disturb" — to interrupt or upset. (परेशान करना)

NOTE

• The verb "deepen" is formed from the adjective "deep" + the suffix "-en". Similar verbs: strengthen, widen, lengthen, sharpen, brighten, soften, harden.

question: Which mineral is present in high amounts in milk, seafood, nuts and whole grains, which helps in bone health and in the repair processes of our body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Phosphorus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Phosphorus (फॉस्फोरस) is present in high amounts in milk, seafood, nuts and whole grains, and it supports bone health and the body's repair processes.

• It is the second most abundant mineral in the human body after calcium. About 85% of the body's phosphorus is stored in the bones and teeth as calcium phosphate / hydroxyapatite.

• Functions: formation of bones and teeth, production of ATP (the energy currency of the cell), building DNA and RNA, and maintenance of acid-base balance in the blood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Fluoride (फ्लोराइड) — protects tooth enamel from decay; excess causes fluorosis. Chief source is drinking water, not milk or nuts.

• Option 2 Potassium (पोटैशियम) — an electrolyte for nerve impulses, muscle contraction and blood pressure control; found in bananas, potatoes and citrus fruits.

• Option 4 Zinc (जिंक) — needed for immunity, wound healing and enzyme action; deficiency stunts growth.

NOTE

• Phosphorus: symbol P, atomic number 15, Group 15 of the periodic table; discovered by Hennig Brand (1669).

• Macro-minerals required in large quantities: calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, sodium, potassium, chlorine, sulphur.

• Deficiency of vitamin D impairs the absorption of both calcium and phosphorus, leading to rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

question: What is capital expenditure?
option_1: The amount of money spent on healthcare programmes
option_2: The amount of money spent on repaying loans
option_3: The amount of money spent on subsidies for farmers
option_4: The amount of money spent on the development of infrastructure
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The amount of money spent on the development of infrastructure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Capital expenditure (पूंजीगत व्यय) is government spending that either creates assets or reduces liabilities. Building roads, railways, ports, bridges, schools, hospitals and other infrastructure is the classic example.

• Capital expenditure is productive in nature — it raises the economy's productive capacity and has a high fiscal multiplier, generating employment and future income.

• Examples of capital expenditure: construction of infrastructure, purchase of machinery and equipment, acquisition of land and buildings, loans given by the Centre to States/PSUs, and repayment of the principal of loans.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 and 3 — spending on healthcare programmes and subsidies to farmers is revenue expenditure: it neither creates an asset nor reduces a liability, and it recurs every year.

• Option 2 — this is a trap: repayment of the principal of a loan is capital expenditure, but payment of interest on debt is revenue expenditure. The option as worded ("money spent on repaying loans") is not the defining example the question seeks; infrastructure creation is.

NOTE

• Revenue expenditure: salaries, pensions, subsidies, interest payments, grants for current use — day-to-day running of government.

• Capital receipts (borrowings, disinvestment, recovery of loans) vs revenue receipts (taxes, fees, dividends).

• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts (excluding borrowings); Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts.

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the Annual Financial Statement.

question: Which physiographic division of India from the following is formed of alluvial soil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The Northern Plains.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Northern Plains (उत्तरी मैदान) of India are formed entirely of alluvial soil deposited over millions of years by the three great river systems — the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra — and their tributaries.

• The plains stretch for about 2,400 km from west to east with an average width of 150–300 km, and are among the most densely populated and agriculturally productive regions of the world.

• Alluvial soil is rich in potash, phosphoric acid and lime but deficient in nitrogen and organic matter; it is ideal for wheat, rice, sugarcane and pulses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Peninsular Plateau is made largely of old crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks and is covered mostly by black (regur) soil and red soil.

• The Himalayan Mountains are young fold mountains with thin, immature mountain/forest soils.

• The Islands (Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep) are of volcanic/tectonic and coral origin respectively.

NOTE

• India's six physiographic divisions: (1) The Himalayan Mountains, (2) The Northern Plains, (3) The Peninsular Plateau, (4) The Indian Desert, (5) The Coastal Plains, (6) The Islands.

• Divisions of the Northern Plains: Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar (older alluvium, contains kankar) and Khadar (newer alluvium, more fertile).

• The Northern Plains are further divided into the Punjab Plain, the Ganga Plain and the Brahmaputra Plain.

question: Laterite soil develops as a result of which of the following reasons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Leaching.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Laterite soil develops in areas of high temperature combined with heavy rainfall. The intense rain causes leaching (निक्षालन) — water percolating downward washes away the soluble lime and silica, leaving behind insoluble oxides of iron and aluminium.

• This residual concentration of iron oxide gives laterite soil its characteristic red to reddish-brown colour.

• Laterite soil is generally acidic, poor in nitrogen, phosphate, calcium and organic matter, but rich in iron and aluminium.

• It is suitable for tea, coffee, cashew nut, rubber and tapioca after adequate manuring, and its hardened blocks are widely used as building bricks (hence the Latin name later = brick).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "High temperature only" is incomplete — laterite formation needs both high temperature and heavy seasonal rainfall causing leaching.

• Option 1 Compaction is the compression of soil particles; Option 4 Sedimentation is the settling of transported material, which forms alluvial soil, not laterite.

NOTE

• Laterite soils occur in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Assam and the hilly areas of the Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.

• Major soil types of India (ICAR classification): alluvial, black (regur), red and yellow, laterite, arid/desert, forest and mountain, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy.

• Black soil is best for cotton; alluvial soil covers the largest area (about 40%) of India.

question: The Bhitargaon Brick temple is a good example of the architecture of which of the following periods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Gupta period.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhitargaon temple in Kanpur district, Uttar Pradesh, is the oldest surviving brick (terracotta) temple in India and is a fine example of Gupta-period architecture (c. 5th century CE).

• It is built entirely of baked bricks and decorated with terracotta panels depicting Hindu deities; it has a tall shikhara over the sanctum, an early example of the Nagara style.

• The Gupta age (c. 320–550 CE) is called the "Golden Age of India" and marks the beginning of formal Hindu temple architecture in stone and brick.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other Gupta temples: Dashavatara Temple, Deogarh (UP); Temple No. 17, Sanchi (MP); Bhitari (UP); Tigawa (MP); Nachna Kuthara (MP).

• Option 1 Mughal period — Indo-Islamic architecture such as the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Humayun's Tomb.

• Option 3 Mauryan period — rock-cut caves of Barabar, the Ashokan pillars and stupas such as Sanchi's core.

• Option 4 Chola period — Dravidian temples like Brihadeeswarar Temple, Thanjavur and the Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram.

NOTE

• Major Gupta rulers: Sri Gupta, Chandragupta I, Samudragupta (the "Indian Napoleon", praised in the Allahabad Pillar inscription by Harisena), Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (visited by the Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien), Kumaragupta I (founder of Nalanda Mahavihara) and Skandagupta (repelled the Hunas).

• The Iron Pillar of Mehrauli, famous for its rust-resistance, is also assigned to the Gupta age.

question: ‘Autobiography of a Yogi’ is the autobiography of _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Paramahansa Yogananda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Autobiography of a Yogi" (first published in 1946) is the life story of Paramahansa Yogananda (1893–1952), the Indian monk who introduced Kriya Yoga and Indian spiritual thought to the West.

• Yogananda founded the Self-Realization Fellowship (SRF) in Los Angeles in 1920 and the Yogoda Satsanga Society of India (YSS) in 1917 at Ranchi.

• The book has been translated into more than 50 languages and is regarded as one of the most influential spiritual books of the 20th century; Steve Jobs famously read it every year.

• His guru was Swami Sri Yukteswar Giri, in the lineage of Lahiri Mahasaya and Mahavatar Babaji.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj (1875, Bombay) and wrote "Satyarth Prakash"; his slogan was "Back to the Vedas".

• Option 3 Ramakrishna Paramahansa was the guru of Swami Vivekananda; his teachings were compiled by "M" as "The Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna".

• Option 4 Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897) and wrote "Raja Yoga", "Karma Yoga", "Jnana Yoga" and "Bhakti Yoga"; his Chicago address at the Parliament of the World's Religions was in 1893.

NOTE

• Famous Indian autobiographies: "The Story of My Experiments with Truth" — M. K. Gandhi; "An Autobiography / Toward Freedom" — Jawaharlal Nehru; "India Wins Freedom" — Maulana Abul Kalam Azad; "Wings of Fire" — A. P. J. Abdul Kalam; "My Country My Life" — L. K. Advani.

question: The Paika dance of Jharkhand is usually performed by the ___________ tribe to welcome specially honoured guests or during a religious procession (shobha yatra).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Munda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Paika (पाइका) dance is a martial folk dance of Jharkhand, performed chiefly by the Munda tribe to welcome distinguished guests and during religious processions (shobha yatra).

• The word "Paika" comes from the Sanskrit padatika, meaning foot soldier. Dancers carry a sword and shield, wear turbans and ankle bells, and perform vigorous mock-combat movements.

• Accompanying instruments include the dhol, nagara, shehnai and narsinga.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Major tribes of Jharkhand: Munda, Santhal, Oraon, Ho, Kharia, Bhumij, Birhor, Asur and the PVTGs such as Sauria Paharia and Birhor.

• Other folk dances of Jharkhand: Chhau (Seraikela Chhau — also an ICH element), Jhumar, Domkach, Karma, Firkal, Mundari and Santhali dances.

• The Santhal are the largest tribe of Jharkhand and perform the Santhali/Dong dances; the Oraon are known for Jadur and Karma.

NOTE

• Birsa Munda (1875–1900), revered as "Dharti Aaba", led the Ulgulan (Great Tumult) Munda rebellion; 15 November, his birth anniversary, is celebrated as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas and is also the foundation day of Jharkhand (2000).

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000; capital Ranchi.

question: As per the Census of India 2011, which state recorded a negative population growth rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Nagaland was the only state to record a negative decadal population growth rate — about −0.58% (some sources give −0.47%) for 2001–2011.

• Nagaland's population fell from about 19.9 lakh (2001) to about 19.79 lakh (2011). The abnormally high growth of 64.5% recorded in 1991–2001 is believed to have been inflated, and the correction shows up as a negative figure in 2011.

• Nagaland thus had the lowest decadal growth rate among the states in Census 2011.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 (15th Census since 1872, 7th after Independence): total population 121.09 crore; decadal growth 17.7%; density 382 persons/sq km; sex ratio 943; literacy 74.04%.

• Highest decadal growth among states: Meghalaya (27.9%); lowest (positive): Kerala (4.9%).

• Most populous state: Uttar Pradesh; least populous: Sikkim. Highest density: Bihar (1,106); lowest: Arunachal Pradesh (17).

• Highest literacy: Kerala (94%); lowest: Bihar (61.8%). Highest sex ratio: Kerala (1,084); lowest: Haryana (879).

NOTE

• The motto of Census 2011 was "Our Census, Our Future"; the Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs, as per the Census Act, 1948.

• The first complete Census of India was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon; the first (non-synchronous) attempt was in 1872 under Lord Mayo.

question: In March 2023, Rajasthan became the first state in India to provide right to ___ for its people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. health.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In March 2023, the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly passed the Rajasthan Right to Health Bill, 2022, making Rajasthan the first state in India to guarantee a legal Right to Health to its residents.

• The Act entitles every resident to free emergency treatment and care at all public health institutions and at designated private facilities, without prepayment of fees or charges.

• It provides for State and District Health Authorities and a grievance-redressal mechanism; the Chief Minister at that time was Ashok Gehlot.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — the Right to Education is a national right under Article 21A (inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002) and the RTE Act, 2009, not a Rajasthan-first initiative.

• Rajasthan has been a pioneer in rights-based laws: the Right to Information (RTI) movement (MKSS, Aruna Roy) began there, and the state also enacted the Right to Hearing Act, 2012.

NOTE

• Related constitutional provisions: Article 21 (right to life, judicially expanded to include the right to health), Article 47 (Directive Principle — duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and public health).

• Major central health schemes: Ayushman Bharat – PM-JAY (2018), National Health Mission, PM Jan Arogya Yojana, Mission Indradhanush.

• Rajasthan: largest state by area; capital Jaipur; formed in its present shape on 1 November 1956.

question: Who was the political guru of Subhas Chandra Bose?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Chittaranjan Das.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das (1870–1925) was the political guru (राजनीतिक गुरु) of Subhas Chandra Bose.

• After resigning from the Indian Civil Service in 1921, Bose returned to India and joined C. R. Das in Bengal, working as the editor of Das's newspaper "Forward" and later as Chief Executive Officer of the Calcutta Corporation when Das became its first Mayor in 1924.

• C. R. Das, along with Motilal Nehru, founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 to contest elections and enter the legislative councils.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 M. G. Ranade was a moderate leader, founder of the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha and the Prarthana Samaj; he is regarded as the political guru of Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

• Option 2 Mahatma Gandhi was the political guru of Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Patel; Gandhi's own political mentor was Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

• Bose differed sharply with Gandhi and resigned as Congress President in 1939 after winning at Tripuri against Gandhi's nominee Pattabhi Sitaramayya, and formed the Forward Bloc (1939).

NOTE

• Subhas Chandra Bose: born 23 January 1897 at Cuttack (Odisha); Janata Nayak/Parakram Diwas is observed on his birth anniversary.

• He reorganised the Azad Hind Fauj (INA) in 1943 and formed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) at Singapore; slogans — "Give me blood and I will give you freedom", "Jai Hind", "Dilli Chalo".

• He addressed Gandhiji as the "Father of the Nation" in a radio broadcast in 1944.

question: Which state has the maximum number of Jute mills (as of 2022)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• West Bengal has the maximum number of jute mills in India — the great majority of the country's roughly 90+ jute mills are located there, mostly in a narrow belt along the Hooghly river near Kolkata.

• Reasons for this concentration: proximity to the jute-producing areas of the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta, abundant water for retting and processing, cheap water and rail transport, plentiful labour from Bihar, Odisha and UP, and the port of Kolkata for export.

• India is the largest producer of raw jute in the world, while Bangladesh is the largest exporter of jute goods.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other jute-producing/processing states: Bihar, Assam, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Meghalaya and Tripura.

• The first jute mill in India was set up at Rishra (near Serampore), West Bengal, in 1855.

• Jute is called the "golden fibre"; it needs a hot and humid climate (25–35°C), 150–250 cm rainfall and well-drained alluvial soil.

NOTE

• The National Jute Board (Kolkata) and the Jute Corporation of India (price-support agency) work under the Ministry of Textiles.

• The Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing Commodities) Act, 1987 mandates the use of jute bags for packing foodgrains and sugar.

• Jute Technology Mission and JUTE-SMART (online supply-chain platform) are important government initiatives.

question: What is the main role of commercial banks in the economy?
option_1: To promote economic growth and development
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To promote economic growth and development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main role of commercial banks is to mobilise savings by accepting deposits and to channel them into productive investment through loans and advances, thereby promoting economic growth and development.

• Key functions:

◦ Primary functions — accepting deposits (savings, current, fixed, recurring) and advancing loans (cash credit, overdraft, term loans, discounting of bills).

◦ Secondary functions — agency services (collection of cheques, payment of bills, remittances) and general utility services (lockers, letters of credit, foreign exchange dealings).

• Through credit creation they expand the money supply (money multiplier), finance industry, agriculture and trade, and help in capital formation and employment generation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — regulating the stock market is the job of SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India, 1988; statutory in 1992).

• Option 3 — controlling inflation through monetary policy is the job of the RBI, guided by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) with an inflation target of 4% (±2%).

• Option 4 — managing the country's foreign exchange reserves is also an RBI function under FEMA, 1999.

NOTE

• RBI: established 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934; nationalised 1949; headquarters Mumbai; first Governor Sir Osborne Smith, first Indian Governor C. D. Deshmukh.

• Bank nationalisation: 14 banks in 1969 and 6 more in 1980.

• Quantitative tools of monetary policy: CRR, SLR, repo rate, reverse repo rate, bank rate, open market operations, MSF.

question: Gaur Maria, a dance form of the state of ____________, is a famous art form of joy and invocation. It is a group dance and both men and women take part in this dance enthusiastically.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Chhattisgarh.

• Gaur Maria is a famous tribal dance of Chhattisgarh, performed by the Muria/Maria Gonds of the Bastar region.

• The name comes from the gaur (Indian bison): male dancers wear head-dresses fitted with bison horns and plumes, while women dance with iron rods and ankle bells, moving in a circle to the beat of dhol and mandar.

• It is a group dance of joy and invocation in which both men and women take part enthusiastically — exactly as described in the question.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Chhattisgarh: Panthi (Satnami community), Raut Nacha, Karma, Saila, Sua/Suwa, Pandwani (a narrative folk-singing form popularised by Teejan Bai).

• Option 1 Maharashtra — Lavani, Tamasha, Dhangari Gaja, Koli.

• Option 2 Rajasthan — Ghoomar, Kalbelia (UNESCO ICH), Chari, Bhavai, Terah Taali.

question: Born on ____________, Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi whose birthday is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti, successfully led India’s non-violence movement against the British.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 2 October 1869.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 at Porbandar, Gujarat. His father Karamchand Gandhi was the diwan of Porbandar and his mother was Putlibai.

• His birthday is celebrated in India as Gandhi Jayanti, a national holiday, and worldwide as the International Day of Non-Violence, declared by the UN General Assembly in 2007.

• He was assassinated on 30 January 1948 at Birla House, Delhi; the day is observed as Martyrs' Day (Shaheed Diwas).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Gandhiji returned to India from South Africa in 1915; his political mentor was Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

• His major movements: Champaran Satyagraha (1917) — indigo farmers of Bihar; Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918); Kheda Satyagraha (1918); Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22); Civil Disobedience / Dandi March (1930); Quit India Movement (1942).

• Titles: "Mahatma" given by Rabindranath Tagore; "Father of the Nation" used by Subhas Chandra Bose; "Bapu" by the people.

NOTE

• Gandhiji's works: autobiography "The Story of My Experiments with Truth", "Hind Swaraj" (1909); journals — "Young India", "Harijan", "Navjivan", "Indian Opinion".

• Ashrams: Phoenix Settlement and Tolstoy Farm (South Africa), Sabarmati Ashram (1917, Ahmedabad) and Sevagram Ashram (1936, Wardha).

• He presided over only one Congress session — Belgaum, 1924.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Cabinet Committee?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Committee on Conflicts among Ministers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There is no Cabinet Committee on "Conflicts among Ministers". It is not among the standing Cabinet Committees constituted by the Prime Minister.

• Cabinet Committees are extra-constitutional bodies (not mentioned in the Constitution) set up under the Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules, 1961. They are constituted by the Prime Minister, who decides their number, composition and functions.

• The eight standing Cabinet Committees are:

◦ Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)

◦ Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs (CCPA) — the "super-cabinet"

◦ Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)

◦ Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS)

◦ Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs

◦ Cabinet Committee on Accommodation

◦ Cabinet Committee on Investment and Growth

◦ Cabinet Committee on Employment and Skill Development

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Prime Minister chairs the ACC, CCPA, CCEA, CCS, Cabinet Committee on Investment and Growth, and the Cabinet Committee on Employment and Skill Development. The Committee on Parliamentary Affairs and the Committee on Accommodation are chaired by senior Cabinet Ministers.

• Membership is normally 3 to 8 members, mostly Cabinet Ministers; non-members can be invited when needed.

NOTE

• Constitutional articles on the Council of Ministers: Article 74 (Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President), Article 75 (appointment, tenure, collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha), Article 77 (conduct of business of the Government of India).

• The word "Cabinet" was inserted in the Constitution by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 in Article 352.

question: Who founded the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan to promote education and culture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Dr. Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan was founded in 1938 at Mumbai by Dr. K. M. Munshi (Kulapati Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi) with the blessings of Mahatma Gandhi, to promote Indian education, culture and values.

• Its motto is "आ नो भद्रा: क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वत:" ("Let noble thoughts come to us from every side" — Rig Veda).

• K. M. Munshi was a freedom fighter, lawyer, Gujarati writer and member of the Constituent Assembly's Drafting Committee. He served as India's Minister of Food and Agriculture (launching Van Mahotsav in 1950) and later as Governor of Uttar Pradesh (1952–57).

• He also led the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple after Independence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 Dr. Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj (1867, Bombay).

• Option 3 Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society (1905); he was Gandhiji's political guru.

• Option 4 Dr. B. R. Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924), the Independent Labour Party (1936), the Scheduled Castes Federation (1942) and the People's Education Society (1945).

NOTE

• Munshi's famous Gujarati novels: "Prithivi Vallabh", "Jay Somnath", "Patan ni Prabhuta"; his English works include "The End of an Era".

• Members of the Drafting Committee (1947): B. R. Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K. M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rao and T. T. Krishnamachari.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution secures a living wage and a decent standard of life with social and cultural opportunities for all workers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Article 43.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 43 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP), directs the State to secure for all workers — agricultural, industrial or otherwise — a living wage, conditions of work ensuring a decent standard of life, and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities.

• It also directs the State to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas.

• Article 43 is a Gandhian principle among the DPSPs, contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 39 — certain principles of policy: adequate means of livelihood, equitable distribution of material resources, equal pay for equal work for men and women, protection of the health of workers and children.

• Article 40 — organisation of village panchayats as units of self-government (Gandhian principle).

• Article 41 — right to work, education and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement.

• Article 43A (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976) — participation of workers in the management of industries.

• Article 43B (added by the 97th Amendment, 2011) — promotion of co-operative societies.

NOTE

• DPSPs are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland; they are non-justiciable (Article 37) but "fundamental in the governance of the country".

• Classification of DPSPs: Socialistic (39, 41, 42, 43, 47), Gandhian (40, 43, 43B, 46, 47, 48) and Liberal-Intellectual (44, 45, 48, 48A, 49, 50, 51).

• In Minerva Mills (1980) the Supreme Court held that harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs is part of the basic structure.

question: Which of the following is a white to yellowish solid with a weak aromatic odour purified by the process of sublimation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anthracene.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anthracene (C₁₄H₁₀) is a colourless to white or pale-yellow crystalline solid with a weak aromatic odour. It is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) made of three linearly fused benzene rings.

• It is obtained from coal tar and is purified by sublimation — the process in which a solid changes directly into vapour on heating and back into solid on cooling, without passing through the liquid state.

• Anthracene shows blue fluorescence under ultraviolet light and is used to make anthraquinone dyes (alizarin), wood preservatives, insecticides and organic scintillators/LEDs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Titanyl refers to the TiO²⁺ group found in compounds such as titanyl sulphate — not an aromatic solid.

• Option 2 Orthovanadate is the VO₄³⁻ anion of vanadic acid salts — an inorganic ion.

• Option 4 Dysprosium (Dy) is a lanthanide metal, atomic number 66, used in magnets and control rods — a silvery metal, not aromatic.

NOTE

• Substances commonly purified by sublimation: camphor, naphthalene, iodine, ammonium chloride, benzoic acid, anthracene, dry ice (solid CO₂).

• Other purification techniques: distillation (liquids with different boiling points), fractional distillation, crystallisation, chromatography and filtration.

• Related PAHs: naphthalene (2 rings), anthracene and phenanthrene (3 rings), benzopyrene (5 rings, a known carcinogen in tobacco smoke).

question: TN Rajarathnam Pillai is a player of which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Nadaswaram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• T. N. Rajarathnam Pillai (1898–1956) was the most celebrated exponent of the Nadaswaram (नादस्वरम), the classical double-reed wind instrument of South India.

• The Nadaswaram is regarded as the loudest non-brass acoustic instrument in the world and is considered mangala vadya (auspicious), indispensable at South Indian temple rituals and weddings. It is usually accompanied by the thavil (a barrel drum) and the ottu (drone).

• Rajarathnam Pillai was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1953) and is credited with raising the Nadaswaram from temple music to the concert platform.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Ghatam — an earthen pot percussion instrument of Carnatic music; famous exponent Vikku Vinayakram.

• Option 2 Sarangi — a bowed string instrument of Hindustani music; famous exponents Pandit Ram Narayan and Ustad Sultan Khan.

• Option 4 Shehnai — the North Indian double-reed wind instrument; its greatest exponent was Ustad Bismillah Khan (Bharat Ratna, 2001).

NOTE

• Classification of Indian musical instruments (Natya Shastra):

◦ Tata Vadya (string) — veena, sitar, sarod, sarangi, violin

◦ Sushira Vadya (wind) — flute, shehnai, nadaswaram, harmonium

◦ Avanaddha Vadya (membrane/percussion) — tabla, mridangam, pakhawaj, thavil

◦ Ghana Vadya (solid/idiophone) — ghatam, jaltarang, manjira, morsing

• Other Carnatic instruments: veena, mridangam, kanjira, morsing, violin.
